sections.h2: How can a Paramus owner get a house sold fast?
sections.html:
Three routes lead to a closing here: an agent listing, a private sale, or an investor who takes a house left as is. All three finish at the same borough inspection and the same deed filings, so what changes is the amount of preparation you do first.

Paramus is a borough in central Bergen County, roughly 15 to 20 miles northwest of Midtown Manhattan. The borough is best known for its two retail corridors along Routes 4 and 17, yet it is also a suburban bedroom community of New York City. To compare the routes, start with this short list:

  • Check whether any permit for past work on the house is still open at the Building Department.
  • Decide whether you can wait for a conventional buyer's financing and inspection period.
  • Locate the deed, a payoff letter from your lender and, if you inherited, the estate papers.
  • Have a closing attorney confirm which deed forms the sale needs.

Skipping the marketing stage saves weeks. The borough's Certificate of Compliance stays in the path, and Paramus describes it as mandatory for closings.

sections.h2: What sets Paramus apart as a place to sell a house?
sections.html:
Paramus covers 10.5 square miles and was incorporated in April 1922 after it split off from Midland Township, which is now Rochelle Park. It was farm country until the 1950s, when the George Washington Bridge and wider Routes 4 and 17 pulled in shopping centers. Garden State Plaza sits where those two routes cross, and the Census Bureau reports 2022 retail sales in the borough of about $5.45 billion.

The borough names five residential areas: Arcola, Bergen Place, Dunkerhook, Fairway Oaks and Spring Valley. Van Saun County Park (146 acres, with the county zoo) lies on the east side, and Saddle River County Park runs along the west side with a six-mile bike path. Paramus Public Schools run eight schools from pre-kindergarten through grade 12, and Bergen Community College has its main campus in the borough.

Most trips here are by car. The borough counts 121.92 miles of road, including Route 17, Route 4 and Garden State Parkway Interchange 165, and NJ Transit buses reach the Port Authority Bus Terminal and the George Washington Bridge Bus Station. Sellers who live near the highways should expect buyers to ask about traffic noise and commute time, since the Census puts the mean trip to work at 30.8 minutes.

sections.h2: How do Paramus homes and households measure up in Census data?
sections.html:
Paramus skews toward owners and high values: more than four in five homes are occupied by their owners. Treat these Census Bureau numbers as a borough-wide picture rather than a price for any single street.

sections.h2: What does Paramus require before my house can close?
sections.html:
Paramus requires a Certificate of Compliance for any resale or rental, and the borough states that this certificate is mandatory for closings. The Building Department asks sellers to confirm first that every earlier permit has been closed out, then file an application with a $100 fee for a sale.

After the application is accepted, an inspector visits. Resale inspections run weekday mornings from 9:00 to 12:00, and someone needs to be at the house to let the inspector in. The borough's guidelines list what gets checked:

  • Smoke alarms on every level and near bedrooms, plus carbon monoxide detectors near sleeping areas, following the borough's NFPA-based guidelines.
  • A permanent label within 18 inches of the electrical panel and meter if the house has solar panels, a generator or battery storage.
  • The street number visible from the street on the mailbox, front door or garage.
  • Borough-issued garbage and recycling containers on the property with their serial numbers.
  • A fence around any pool.

Open permits cause the most delays. Unpermitted renovations must be permitted and inspected before the certificate is released, and permitted jobs lacking a final inspection hold up the Certificate of Occupancy. The guidelines also ask that open permits be closed a full week ahead of the resale inspection. Call the Building Department at 201-265-2100, extension 2230, for the current process.

sections.h2: Which state charges follow a Paramus sale?
sections.html:
The seller carries the Realty Transfer Fee, which the county collects at recording. The Division of Taxation steps the charge from $2.90 to $6.05 for each $500 of price on sales above $350,000, and a Graduated Percent Fee is layered on once a sale passes $1,000,000. Your closing attorney or title agent can turn the schedule into a dollar figure for your deed.

Estate sales are one common exemption: an executor's deed to an heir following a will is excused, as is a deed between parent and child. Form RTF-1 goes on record with the deed for any seller claiming relief.

Recording also requires a GIT/REP form under N.J.S.A. 54A:8-9, so the State can tell whether a seller living outside New Jersey owes prepaid income tax. Whoever signs the deed completes it, and only sheriff's sales and bankruptcy trustee sales are left out.

sections.h2: Does a Paramus seller have to disclose flooding?
sections.html:
Yes. Beginning March 20, 2024, the property condition disclosure statement has to carry flood answers before a buyer is committed to the contract: whether the lot falls inside a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area or Moderate Flood Hazard Area, and whatever flood history you personally know.

The Department of Environmental Protection runs a Flood Risk Notification Tool that helps sellers look up the answers. Check your own parcel on that tool instead of assuming the answer. Cash buyers and conventional buyers receive the same disclosure.

sections.h2: How are Paramus property taxes set, and how do I contest them?
sections.html:
Every New Jersey county assesses at 100 percent of market value as of October 1, and the local rate applied to that figure produces your bill. Because Paramus lies in Bergen County, contested assessments go to the Bergen County Board of Taxation.

  • Filing: Form A-1, in the board's hands by April 1.
  • After a revaluation: the cutoff moves to May 1.
  • Large assessments: above $1,000,000 can skip to the State Tax Court.
  • Next level: 45 days to take a board ruling to the Tax Court.

The burden is yours: prove the figure is out of line with market value or with the district's common level range. Ask the Paramus tax collector for your payoff and quarterly status before closing, so any open installment is cleared at the closing table and the buyer inherits no surprise.

faqs.q: Is a borough certificate really required to close a sale in Paramus?
faqs.a: Yes. The borough treats the resale Certificate of Compliance as mandatory at closing. The seller applies to the Building Department, pays $100 and passes the inspection.

faqs.q: What happens if I made changes to the house without permits?
faqs.a: The resale certificate is withheld until the missing permits are applied for and the work is inspected. Permitted work that never received a final inspection holds up the Certificate of Occupancy.

faqs.q: Is the New Jersey transfer fee my bill in Paramus?
faqs.a: The seller. It is a state charge on the seller at recording, sized by the price brackets on the Division of Taxation schedule.

faqs.q: At what point must a buyer receive flood information?
faqs.a: Before the buyer is committed to the purchase contract. The statement covers FEMA flood zone status and any flood problems the seller knows about.

faqs.q: How late can I file a Paramus assessment appeal?
faqs.a: April 1, or May 1 following a revaluation or reassessment, and the petition must reach the county board by then. Ask the Bergen County Board of Taxation for the form and current filing steps.
